title: SDK behavior spec: pagination edge cases, retry contract, and streaming interoperability
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: PRD-level specification and acceptance criteria for SDK client behaviour across Python, TypeScript, and Go. This ticket captures clarified requirements after engineering and design syncs and scopes what shall land in the next SDK release window. Goals: 1) Define a single pagination contract (cursor-first) with language idiomatic helpers; 2) Define a shared retry contract (idempotency rules, backoff, and instrumentation hooks); 3) Define streaming API semantics (connectivity, resume, cancellation/backpressure) and compatibility guarantees; 4) Specify deprecation & compatibility policy for SDKs so server updates don't break published clients. Non-goals: shipping language-specific async-first micro-libraries or wire-level protocol changes (e.g., replacing HTTP streaming with websockets) - those are out of scope for this sprint.
requirements_summary: Pagination: cursor-based primary contract with optional next_page_token, server-driven page_size bounds, and client iterators/generators for sync/async languages
Retries: uniform client-side retry policy with explicit retryable error set, exponential backoff with jitter, max_attempts and opt-out hooks; per-request idempotency key support

Streaming: standardize on HTTP chunked/line-delimited JSON for hosted API; SDKs must expose the same high-level streaming primitives (events iterator, on_message callback, cancel/token), with resume tokens where server supports it
Compatibility: semantic versioning per-language; minor releases may add helpers but not break signatures; breaking changes require 3-month deprecation window and automated migration guide
Observability: SDKs must emit structured telemetry points for request/response lifecycle, retry events, stream reconnects, and pagination boundaries
language_contracts: Python: provide sync iterator (iter_responses) and async async_generator (aiter_responses); SDK will surface `page_size`, `page_token` and a convenience `all()` helper that streams items lazily
TypeScript: offer Promise-based paginated helpers and async iterable for streams (`for await (const item of client.listX())`), with explicit AbortSignal cancellation support
Go: idiomatic channel-based streaming helper plus synchronous Page() that returns a typed pager object; context.Context must control cancellation and timeouts
pagination_details: Server returns `next_page_token` when additional results exist; empty string or missing token => end-of-list
Clients must guard against duplicate items across page boundaries (idempotent de-duplication helper available in SDK), and expose raw tokens for advanced users
Minimum page_size accepted by server documented; SDKs must validate and clamp client-specified values to server limits with a visible warning log
Pagination helpers must support an optional `limit` argument that caps total items returned across pages
retry_policy: Retryable errors: transient network errors (connection reset/timeouts), 429 (rate limit) with Retry-After respected, and 5xx server errors except 501/505
Non-retryable errors: 4xx client errors indicating invalid request payloads or permission issues
Backoff: exponential base 100ms, multiplier 2.0, max backoff 8s, full jitter recommended; SDKs expose configuration to change base/multiplier/max
Idempotency: requests that mutate state must accept an `idempotency_key`; SDK will not auto-retry unsafe mutates unless explicit idempotency key present
Telemetry: emit 'retry_attempt' event with original error, attempt_count, and delay_ms for each retry
streaming_semantics: Transport: use HTTP chunked responses with newline-delimited JSON frames for hosted API; SDKs will parse frames and yield typed events
Lifecycle: streams surface `open`, `message`, `error`, `close` events; SDK helpers should provide both pull (iterator) and push (callback) patterns
Cancel/Backpressure: client cancel signals (AbortSignal/Context/cancel_token) must stop processing and close underlying connection promptly
Reconnect & resume: when server provides resume_token, SDK must attempt a single transparent reconnect and resume from the token; if resume fails, surface a recoverable error with guidance
Partial failures: per-message errors must be surfaced inline (as error events) without tearing down the whole stream unless the server indicates fatal state
compatibility_policy: Versioning: follow semver for SDKs. Patch = bug fixes, Minor = new helpers/backwards-compatible additions, Major = breaking changes
Deprecation timeline: announce breaking changes 90 days prior; maintain compatibility shims for two minor releases where feasible
Server-driven changes: runtime may add optional fields; clients must ignore unknown fields by default and expose raw payload for advanced parsing
Automated tests: each SDK must include smoke tests that validate pagination, retry behavior and stream reconnection against the staging sandbox
acceptance_criteria: API contracts doc published in Confluence with example code for Python/TS/Go
Engineering PRs created for SDK skeletons with language-specific helpers and basic tests
End-to-end smoke test demonstrating pagination across multiple pages and `limit` enforcement in all three SDKs
Retry behavior validated by fault-injection tests (simulate 500 and network timeouts) and telemetry events verified in staging
Streaming: client able to consume a long-running stream, cancel mid-stream via signal/context and resume using a provided resume_token in at least two SDKs
Compatibility: compatibility.md added to SDK repos describing upgrade/downgrade expectations and deprecation window
Docs: developer docs and migration guide for previously-unversioned clients published alongside SDK release notes
